name: WPC Smart Inventory Manager for WooCommerce
author: WPClever

sections.description:
WPC Smart Inventory Manager provides a dedicated Stock Central dashboard for WooCommerce stores, allowing you to view, edit, and manage all product inventory from a single screen — without navigating to individual product pages.

Key Features

  • Stock Central Dashboard – A centralized table view for all product stock data, including simple products, variable products, and their variations.
  • Inline Quick Editing – Edit stock quantity, SKU, barcode (GTIN), regular price, sale price, backorder settings, and manage stock toggle directly from the table.
  • Bulk Stock Actions – Select multiple products and apply bulk actions: set stock to a specific value, increase/decrease by amount, enable/disable manage stock.
  • Stock Status Filters – Filter products by stock status (in stock, low stock, out of stock), product type, and manage stock setting.
  • Stock Change History – Every stock change is logged with old/new values, change amount, reason, user, and timestamp for full traceability.
  • Stock Trend Charts – View stock history as a visual chart to identify trends and patterns over time.
  • Dashboard Alerts Widget – A WordPress dashboard widget showing low stock and out of stock product counts at a glance.
  • CSV Export – Export your current inventory view (with active filters) to a CSV file for offline analysis or reporting.
  • Product Type Support – Configure which product types appear in Stock Central (simple, variable, grouped, external, or custom types from other plugins).
  • Customizable Columns – Choose which extra columns to display: SKU, barcode, regular price, sale price, backorders, manage stock, sold individually, and more.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Navigate to Stock Central in the WordPress admin menu to view all products.
  3. Click on any field to edit it inline — changes are saved via AJAX instantly.
  4. Use the filters and search to narrow down products, then apply bulk actions as needed.
  5. Enable Profit Intelligence in settings to track costs and view profit analytics.

sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  3. Ensure WooCommerce is installed and activated.
  4. Navigate to WPClever > Inventory Manager to configure settings.
  5. Navigate to Stock Central to start managing your inventory.
